newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Playboy sees soft Q2 advertising market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Playboy sees soft Q2 advertising market.

text.p: Playboy Enterprises Inc expects first-quarter advertising softness to spill over into its second fiscal quarter ending December 31, said Christie Hefner, chairman and chief executive officer.

"We'll certainly have a soft first half compared to last year," Hefner said on Friday in an interview. "The whole market is soft, and we're not doing better than the market in terms of (advertising) pages."
Playboy Magazine recorded lower ad revenue in the first quarter of $5.7 million, down from $6.7 million a year ago.

For all of fiscal 1996, the flagship magazine's ad revenues were $27.4 million, compared to $27.6 million the prior year. Ad revenues from the magazine accounted for about 10 percent of the company's total fiscal 1996 revenues.

Hefner cited weakness in consumer electronics, which curtailed advertisements for computers, televisions and other equipment. She added, "Consumption of distilled spirits has not been strong, and tobacco is under its own pressures. It's not a great ad environment."
The second half of FY97 looks to be better than the first, said Hefner, adding "beyond that, it's hard to predict."
Of Playboy's total fiscal 1996 revenues, publishing accounted for $132.9 million, entertainment $64.8 million, product marketing $7.1 million and catalog $71.7 million.
Playboy's entertainment group is performing well, Hefner said. During the first quarter, Playboy TV revenues rose 17 percent because of a robust satellite direct-to-home business, Hefner said.
The company this month is adding a Latin American television network and scouting for other countries in Europe and the Far East for similar expansion.
Cable is still a slow growing business in the U.S. and will continue in that manner throughout fiscal 1997, Hefner said.

"But the combination of the domestic impact of the direct-to-home growth with quicker-than-expected growth in the development of markets for Playboy networks overseas has helped us produce good results over the last six quarters," she said.

New revenue sources for the company will come through the agreements for co-production of low budget movies, a pay site on the Internet and the sale of branded cigars. Hefner also said the Playboy Casino, in which the company has about a 15 percent stake, is expected to open next summer on the Greek island of Rhodes.
Playboy was unchanged in trading on Friday at 12.
Gruntal & Co analyst Rita Zanella, who recently reiterated her buy recommendation on Playboy with an outperform rating, called the stock undervalued. Her 12-month price target on the stock is $18.
